title: 5 levels, 5 bosses, 7 weapons: what an AI-assisted solo dev workflow looks like after a few weeks
author: tooavg
selftext:
Bonkwood is a 2D brawler in Godot 4 that runs in the browser. Combat is inspired by Brawlhalla, but it's all PvE against forest monsters and crowned bosses. How it's made: - Code: Claude writes the GDScript. I decide what the game should be, playtest every build and give feedback. All the gameplay values live in JSON files so I can tune them myself. - Art: backgrounds, enemies and bosses are generated with Gemini, then cut out and cleaned up with small Python scripts. The weapon art is drawn as SVG by code. - Music and sound: generated with scripts too, plus some free sound packs. - Testing: real playtesters. Most of today's changes came straight from their feedback (enemy attack warnings, smaller aggro range, volume settings). What worked: fast iteration. I can ask for a feature, play it ten minutes later and throw it away if it doesn't feel right. What didn't: the AI likes to add systems. Several times I had to say "no, simpler". Visual consistency between AI-generated assets is also still the weakest part. Free in the browser: [https://vestom.itch.io/bonkwood](https://vestom.itch.io/bonkwood)

 Happy to asnwer about the workflow.
